_note: English tongue twisters for /zungenbrecher, all traditional (folk rhymes, public domain). Each one is first read out (slowly, then at speed), then the learner repeats it and gets points per word – the same scoring as /aussprache-check. focus: sound ids from src/lib/ausspracheTipps.js. hint: what the twister means, in simple English. Ids are the old slot ids (content-plan §1.3); the German set had 25, this one has 22 (quality over quantity). `audio` is set to true by scripts/generate-zungenbrecher-audio.mjs once public/audio/zungenbrecher/<id>-langsam.mp3 and <id>.mp3 exist; until then the browser voice reads them. mascot (optional): an animal of the crew is in the twister, so it pops up on the card (bruno, regi, hamsti, quaki). mini (optional): another animal in the twister, so a small Mini-Crew sticker (src/lib/minis.js) sits on the card. dialect (optional): the same twister in a dialect, voiced as <id>-<slug(dialect.name)>.mp3, only for listening and never scored; none in the English set yet.

sentences.text: Fresh fried fish, fish fresh fried, fried fish fresh, fish fried fresh.
sentences.hint: Fish that is fresh and fried, said in four different orders.

sentences.text: Red lorry, yellow lorry.
sentences.hint: A lorry is a big vehicle that carries goods (US: truck). One is red, one is yellow.

sentences.text: Toy boat, toy boat, toy boat.
sentences.hint: A toy boat is a small boat that children play with. Say it fast!

sentences.text: Fred fed Ted bread, and Ted fed Fred bread.
sentences.hint: Fred gives Ted some bread, and then Ted gives Fred some bread.

sentences.text: A big black bug bit a big black bear.
sentences.hint: A bug is a small insect. It bit (past of bite) a big black bear.

sentences.text: I scream, you scream, we all scream for ice cream.
sentences.hint: To scream means to shout very loudly. “I scream” and “ice cream” sound almost the same.

sentences.text: Red leather, yellow leather.
sentences.hint: Leather is the skin of an animal. We use it for shoes and bags.

sentences.text: Which witch is which?
sentences.hint: which (the question word) and witch (a woman with magic powers in old stories) sound the same.

sentences.text: She sells seashells by the seashore.
sentences.hint: A woman sells shells from the sea, on the beach.

sentences.text: Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers.
sentences.hint: A peck is an old measure, about 9 litres. Pickled peppers are kept in vinegar.

sentences.text: How much wood would a woodchuck chuck if a woodchuck could chuck wood?
sentences.hint: A woodchuck is an animal from North America. To chuck means to throw.

sentences.text: Round the rugged rock the ragged rascal ran.
sentences.hint: A rascal is a naughty person. The rock is rugged (rough), and the rascal is ragged (in old, torn clothes).

sentences.text: Six slippery snails slid slowly seaward.
sentences.hint: Snails are small, slow animals with a shell. Seaward means towards the sea.

sentences.text: Six thick thistle sticks.
sentences.hint: A thistle is a wild plant with sharp points.

sentences.text: A proper copper coffee pot.
sentences.hint: A coffee pot made of real copper, a reddish-brown metal.

sentences.text: Fuzzy Wuzzy was a bear. Fuzzy Wuzzy had no hair. Fuzzy Wuzzy wasn't fuzzy, was he?
sentences.hint: Fuzzy means covered in soft hair. A bear with no hair isn't fuzzy at all.

sentences.text: Whether the weather is warm, whether the weather is hot, we have to put up with the weather, whether we like it or not.
sentences.hint: whether (= if) and weather (sun, rain, wind) sound the same. To put up with something means to accept it, even if you don't like it.

sentences.text: Betty Botter bought some butter, but she said the butter's bitter. If I put it in my batter, it will make my batter bitter.
sentences.hint: Batter is a mix of flour, eggs and milk for cakes or pancakes. Bitter is a strong, unpleasant taste.

sentences.text: The sixth sick sheikh's sixth sheep's sick.
sentences.hint: A sheikh is a leader in some Arab countries. The sixth sheikh who is ill has a sixth sheep, and it is ill too.

sentences.text: Irish wristwatch, Swiss wristwatch.
sentences.hint: A wristwatch is a watch you wear on your wrist. One is from Ireland, one is from Switzerland.

sentences.text: Unique New York, unique New York, you know you need unique New York.
sentences.hint: Unique means special, the only one of its kind. New York is a big city in the USA.

sentences.text: I saw Susie sitting in a shoeshine shop. Where she sits, she shines, and where she shines, she sits.
sentences.hint: In a shoeshine shop, someone cleans and polishes your shoes until they shine.
